summary:
Mission Control — Space Mission Design Game is an interactive educational space exploration game that allows players to experience the process of designing, planning, and carrying out space missions using NASA-based tools, technical details, and accurate scientific data.

The project features two playable missions: Earth Observer, where players deploy a CubeSat into Low Earth Orbit to capture and analyze environmental imagery, and Lunar Surveyor, where players navigate a robotic spacecraft to the Moon, establish a polar mapping orbit, and identify potential lunar landing regions.

Players make mission-critical engineering decisions involving launch vehicles, orbital trajectories, spacecraft orientation, scientific instruments, and communications. The game includes self-built animations of rocket takeoff, Earth launch, orbital flight, and lunar landing, bringing the mission experience to life.

Developed entirely by our team, the project combines space science, engineering, interactive simulation, and visual storytelling to make real-world mission design engaging and accessible to beginner and intermediate youth participants.
details:
SMTUltimate is an educational space mission simulator developed in Unity using C# (code was only written using ai to speed up the process, not unknowingly). It introduces young learners to space exploration through two interactive missions: Earth Observer, which deploys a CubeSat into Low Earth Orbit to collect environmental imagery, and Lunar Surveyor, which sends an unmanned orbiter to map the Moon. Players experience the four segments of real space missions: Launch, Space, Ground, and User, making decisions about spacecraft configurations, launch vehicles, orbits, instruments, and communications. The game features interactive 3D spacecraft models, animations, mission simulations, and decision-based feedback. Official NASA 3D models, scientific visualisations, and real-world technologies provide scientific references. By combining realistic scenarios with interactive gameplay, SMTUltimate makes complex aerospace concepts more accessible, encourages scientific curiosity, and helps students understand how space missions operate and contribute to scientific research.
